phrases.ar: الٓمٓ
phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm
phrases.explanation:
These three letters, Alif, Lam and Mim, open the chapter on their own, each letter pronounced by itself. The commentary does not expound them here, because their full discussion was already given at the head of the second chapter, where the same letters first occur, and repeating it would add nothing.

The same applies to the word Allah that follows them: its meaning was likewise explained at the start of the second chapter. What matters here is that the chapter of the Family of Imran begins by affirming the name of Allah and these separate letters, a opening that the early exegetes took as a sign of the chapter's honor.

phrases.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ
phrases.translation: Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining
phrases.explanation:
"There is no god but He" is an announcement by which Allah informs His servants that divinity belongs to Him alone, to the exclusion of every other god or partner set beside Him, and that worship is not fitting or permissible for anyone besides Him. The occasion for this was a delegation from Najran that came to the Messenger and disputed with him about the son of Mary: sixty riders, among them fourteen nobles whose affair was referred to three leaders, the foremost of them being called the Messiah and another the lord.

The Christians argued that the son of Mary is Allah because he raised the dead to life, healed the sick, gave tidings of the unseen, and fashioned a bird out of clay that flew when he breathed into it, all by Allah's permission as a sign for mankind. They argued he is the son of Allah because he had no known father and spoke in the cradle, which no son of Adam before him did. And they argued He is the third of three because He says "We have done, and We have commanded, and We have created, and We have decreed," meaning He, the son of Mary, and Mary.

The Quran descended answering each of these claims, and the same argument covers every creature who disbelieves in Allah and takes another as lord, god, and object of worship, including those who dispute about the son of Mary. When the two scholars of the delegation spoke, the Messenger told them to submit, and they claimed they had already submitted, and he told them they were lying because what held them back was their invocation of a child for Allah, their worship of the cross, and their ascription of divinity to another. "The Ever-Living, All-Sustaining" names Him: the reciters differ over the reading of these two names, some of the regions reading one form and some companions of the readers another, but the meaning is that He lives by His own self and sustains all existence by His own self, needing no son, partner, or helper.

phrases.ar: نَزَّلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقٗا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلَ
phrases.translation: He has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Book in truth, confirming what came before it, as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel
phrases.explanation:
"He has revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it." By "the Book" He means the Quran, sent down with sincerity about the matters in which the People of the Book differed, such as the affair of the son of Mary, and confirming what came before it, meaning the earlier books and messengers.

"As He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before, as a guide for people": the Torah was sent to Moses and the Gospel to the son of Mary before this Book, as an explanation to people of the oneness of Allah and the truth of His messengers, and as a protection for whoever believes in them and acts on what is in them.

phrases.ar: مِن قَبۡلُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانَۗ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٞ شَدِيدٞۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٞ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ
phrases.translation: previously, as a guide for people, and ˹also˺ revealed the Standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺. Surely those who reject Allah’s revelations will suffer a severe torment. For Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment
phrases.explanation:
"And revealed the Standard to distinguish between right and wrong." The Criterion is the separation between truth and falsehood in the matters over which the parties disagreed, such as the affair of the son of Mary. The exegetes differed: some took it as the separation between truth and falsehood about the son of Mary, others as the separation in the rulings of the law, and others as the Quran itself, in which He made the permitted and forbidden clear and fixed His prescriptions. The view that it is the separation He brought about between His Prophet and those who disputed with him is the more fitting, because the verse mentions the Book first and then the Criterion.

"Surely those who reject Allah's revelations will suffer a severe torment. For Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment." Those who disbelieve are those who denied His signs, His proofs of His oneness, and that the son of Mary is His servant, whether they took him as a god or claimed a son for Allah. For them is a severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ شَيۡءٞ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ
phrases.translation: Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah
phrases.explanation:
"Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah." He means that nothing on earth and nothing in heaven is hidden from Him. How could it be hidden from Him, the Knower of all things, what the Christians of Najran want and plot and pretend in their claims about the son of Mary? He has already known their affair and their scheme, and He will not be asked about what He knows in the way a human is asked.

This verse answers those who dispute with the Prophet about the signs of Allah, for nothing of their plotting escapes the Lord of all things.

phrases.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
phrases.translation: He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation:
"He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills." Allah is the One who forms you into shapes in the wombs of your mothers as He wills: He makes one male and another female, one dark and another fair, one complete and another incomplete, and by this He shows that everyone in the wombs belongs to Him and is shaped by Him.

This refutes those who claim divinity for the son of Mary: he was himself shaped in the womb as Allah willed, just as the other children of Adam were, so how could he be a god in that condition? The exegetes differed over the wording, but agreed the womb-shaping proves he was a created servant. "There is no god except Him, the Almighty, All-Wise."

phrases.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
phrases.translation: He is the One Who has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Book, of which some verses are precise—they are the foundation of the Book—while others are elusive. Those with deviant hearts follow the elusive verses seeking ˹to spread˺ doubt through their ˹false˺ interpretations—but none grasps their ˹full˺ meaning except Allah. As for those well-grounded in knowledge, they say, “We believe in this ˹Quran˺—it is all from our Lord.” But none will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason
phrases.explanation:
"It is He who has revealed to you the Book": Allah, from whom nothing is hidden on earth or in heaven, sent down the Quran to His Prophet.

"Of which some verses are precise, they are the foundation of the Book, while others are elusive." The Book contains verses made clear through detailed exposition, the precise ones, and others whose wording resembles one another while their meanings branch apart, the elusive ones. The exegetes differed over what the precise and elusive verses are. Some said the precise are those acted upon, the abrogating verses that establish the rulings, and the elusive are the abrogated ones whose practice was lifted. Others said the precise are what is not abrogated and the elusive what is abrogated. Others said the precise are those in which Allah clarified the permitted and the forbidden. Others said the precise are those admitting only a single interpretation, while the elusive admit several. Others said the precise are the verses whose explanation the scholars know, while the elusive are those whose meaning only Allah reserves to Himself, and this last view agrees most closely with the verse, because everything Allah sent down He explained to His Prophet. As for "they are the foundation of the Book," some said it means the binding element of the Book, others that it means the opening letters of the chapters from which the Quran is brought forth. The grammarians also discussed why the word for "others" carries no nunation, because its singular is feminine.

"Those with deviant hearts follow the elusive verses, seeking to spread doubt through their false interpretations, but none grasps their full meaning except Allah." Deviation means an inclination away from the truth, or doubt, and some said it means the hypocrites. Those in whose hearts is deviation follow the ambiguous verses: they apply the clear to the ambiguous, or twist what is distorted, and they follow the abrogated and the abrogating and ask how the one abrogates the other, seeking discord through their interpretations. Some said the verse means the delegation of the Christians of Najran, who came to the Prophet and disputed with him. But none knows the true interpretation of the elusive except Allah.

"As for those well-grounded in knowledge, they say, We believe in this, it is all from our Lord. But none will be mindful of this except people of reason." The firmly grounded affirm both the precise and the elusive, saying all of it is from their Lord, and only people of intellect take heed. The verse thus draws the line between the one who submits the ambiguous to the Author of the Book and the one who makes the ambiguous a door to discord, and it settles the matter by reserving the knowledge of the elusive to Allah alone while commanding belief in all of it.

phrases.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغۡ قُلُوبَنَا بَعۡدَ إِذۡ هَدَيۡتَنَا وَهَبۡ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
phrases.translation: ˹They say,˺ “Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us. Grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺
phrases.explanation:
"Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Giver of all bounties." This is what the well-grounded in knowledge say: they believe in the elusive verses as they do in the precise, all of it from their Lord.

"Do not let our hearts deviate" means do not make our hearts incline from the straight path even though we incline through our deeds. The Prophet often supplicated, "O You who turn the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." This verse is a supplication in the form of a report: they ask their Lord not to deviate their hearts after He guided them, and to grant them mercy from Himself as support for steadfastness, for He is the Bestower.

phrases.ar: رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ ٱلنَّاسِ لِيَوۡمٖ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُخۡلِفُ ٱلۡمِيعَادَ
phrases.translation: Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the ˹promised˺ Day—about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise.”
phrases.explanation:
"Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the promised Day, about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise." "For a Day" means on a Day, the Day on which Allah gathers His creation for judgment at the place of presentation and reckoning, about which there is no doubt. "The promise" follows the word pattern derived from "promise."

This continues what the well-grounded say: they ask their Lord to gather them on that Day in safety, affirming that Allah does not break His promise, for He is true in what He promises, and His promise is never broken, so the well-grounded say this with certainty and hope.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن تُغۡنِيَ عَنۡهُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـٔٗاۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ وَقُودُ ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.translation: Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah—and they will be the fuel for the Fire
phrases.explanation:
"Neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah, and they will be the fuel for the Fire." "Those who disbelieve" are those who denied the truth they had recognized, the prophethood of the Prophet, among the Jews and their hypocrites and the Arab polytheists. Their wealth and children will not ward off Allah's punishment when it befalls them.

In the Hereafter they are the fuel, the firewood, of the Fire, for nothing they possess can avail them against their Lord, and their end is the Fire whose fuel they will be on that Day, as a recompense for what they denied.

phrases.ar: كَدَأۡبِ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
phrases.translation: Their fate will be like that of the people of Pharaoh and those before them—they all rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment
phrases.explanation:
"Their fate will be like that of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they all rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment." The disbelievers' wealth and children avail them nothing, like the practice of Pharaoh's people and those before them.

The exegetes differed over "like that of": some said it means like their constant practice, others like their deed, others specifically like their denial of the messengers when they denied. All agree on the point: they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them on account of their sins, and Allah is severe in punishment. The like of their fate is the warning for everyone who rejects the signs after they have come to him clearly, and it shows that wealth, children, and numbers do not protect anyone from Allah when His punishment descends, for He is severe in punishment and takes whom He wills for whatever sins He wills.

phrases.ar: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَتُغۡلَبُونَ وَتُحۡشَرُونَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ Tell the disbelievers, “Soon you will be overpowered and driven to Hell—what an evil place to rest!”
phrases.explanation:
"Tell the disbelievers, Soon you will be overpowered and driven to Hell, what an evil place to rest!" The reciters differed: some read "you shall be overcome and driven together" addressed to the disbelievers, others "they shall be overcome and driven together," meaning the Arab polytheists will overcome the Jews. The preferred reading is the second person addressed to the Jews, because the verse "There was a sign for you in two troops" addresses them in the same manner, and the reports confirm it: after the defeat of Quraysh at Badr, the Messenger gathered the Jews of one tribe in their market and told them to beware of Allah, of the like of what befell Quraysh.

"And you shall be driven together" means gathered and conveyed to Hell, and "what an evil place to rest" means what a wretched bed and couch it is.

phrases.ar: قَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةٞ فِي فِئَتَيۡنِ ٱلۡتَقَتَاۖ فِئَةٞ
phrases.translation: Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two armies that met in battle—one fighting for the cause of Allah and the other in denial.
phrases.explanation:
"Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two armies that met in battle, one fighting for the cause of Allah and the other in denial." Say, O Prophet, to the disbelievers among the Jews dwelling in your land: there was for you a token and an indication of the truth of what I tell you about your Prophet and your Book.

"In the two armies" means in two groups and two parties that met for battle, and "army" is the multitude of people. One of the two armies was the Messenger and those who were with him of the believers, a multitude fighting in obedience to Allah and upon His religion. "And the other in denial": the polytheists of Quraysh and their allies. The grammarians noted that "one fighting" stands in the nominative as a new inceptive clause after "in the two armies," and this is like the speech of the Arabs when a predication returns to a counterpart. The reciters also differed over the next phrase: the reciters of Medina read it with the second person, addressed to you the Jews, while most of the reciters of Kufa and Basra and some of the Meccans read it with the third person, that the Muslim army saw the disbelieving multitude as twice its number. That is the sign: the believers were few, about three hundred, while the enemy were near a thousand, yet Allah made the few see the many as double, to strengthen their hearts before the battle. The reports agree that this was at Uhud, when the two armies met, and that the sign was the deliverance of the believers despite their small number, for Allah supports whom He wills and does what He wills with His servants.

phrases.ar: تُقَٰتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُخۡرَىٰ كَافِرَةٞ يَرَوۡنَهُم مِّثۡلَيۡهِمۡ رَأۡيَ ٱلۡعَيۡنِۚ وَٱللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصۡرِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبۡرَةٗ لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
phrases.translation: The believers saw their enemy twice their number. But Allah supports with His victory whoever He wills. Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight
phrases.explanation:
"The believers saw their enemy twice their number." The exegetes differed over which army saw the other as twice itself. Some said the Muslim army saw the polytheists as twice their number, for Allah diminished the polytheists in the sight of the believers. Others, following a reading of a companion, said Allah showed them the number of the polytheists equal to their own, no more. Others said the Muslims saw them as they were in their number, without any doubling. And still others said the disbelieving army saw the Muslim army as twice its own number, which contradicts the outward sense of another verse where Allah says He showed them few in your eyes and you many in theirs.

The people also differed over the number of the polytheists at Badr: some said a thousand, others between nine hundred and a thousand, and others that their number exceeded nine hundred but the Muslims saw it otherwise than it was in reality. An objection about "twice their number" was answered by the Arabic idiom in which a speaker possessing a slave says "I need twice that," meaning himself and his like. The preferred view is that Allah showed the believers the enemy as twice their number, diminished in their eyes, while the enemy were in fact three times their number.

"But Allah supports with His victory whoever He wills. Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight." The seeing was real, with the seeing of the eye, at the meeting of the two armies. And Allah gives victory to whom He wills, so numbers and multitude do not avail against Him, and in this sign there is a lesson for those who have insight.

phrases.ar: زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡبَنِينَ وَٱلۡقَنَٰطِيرِ
phrases.translation: The enjoyment of ˹worldly˺ desires—women, children, treasures of gold and silver, fine horses, cattle, and fertile land—has been made appealing to people.
phrases.explanation:
"The enjoyment of worldly desires, namely women, children, treasures of gold and silver, fine horses, cattle, and fertile land, has been made appealing to people." Allah made fair-seeming to mankind the love of that which they desire, and all of it is enumerated here: women, sons, the hoards, the horses, the cattle, and the crops.

By this He intended a rebuke of the Jews, who prefer the worldly life and love it, while the home of the Hereafter is better and more lasting. One of the early exegetes said that no one has censured the love of the worldly more sharply than the One who created it, for He made it appealing to them and then warned them away from it.

"Treasures of gold and silver" are the hoards, the plural of a hoard of treasure, heaped up and multiplied, as if three became nine, or minted into coins, according to different views. The exegetes differed greatly over the value of the qintar: some said twelve hundred uqiyyah of weight, others twelve hundred dinars, others a thousand dinars or twelve thousand dirhams, others eighty thousand dirhams or a hundred ratl of gold, others seventy thousand, others the hide of a bull filled with gold, and others simply abundant wealth. Some scholars of the language said the Arabs do not fix the qintar by a known weight but call it a certain quantity of weight. The commentator said it ought to be so, for had its quantity been fixed among them, there would not have been among the early exegetes all this disagreement about it, and the correct view is that it is abundant wealth, the one part piled upon the other, as one early exegete said. Some added that the heaped-up treasures are those multiplied and increased beyond measure, and others that they are coins struck and minted, but the meaning returns to abundance of wealth piled up, for the Arabs use the word for any great quantity of gold or silver gathered in one place.

phrases.ar: ٱلۡمُقَنطَرَةِ مِنَ ٱلذَّهَبِ وَٱلۡفِضَّةِ وَٱلۡخَيۡلِ ٱلۡمُسَوَّمَةِ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ وَٱلۡحَرۡثِۗ ذَٰلِكَ مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥ حُسۡنُ ٱلۡمَـَٔابِ
phrases.translation: These are the pleasures of this worldly life, but with Allah is the finest destination
phrases.explanation:
"These are the pleasures of this worldly life, but with Allah is the finest destination." The correct view of the qintar is that it is abundant wealth whose weight is not delimited by an arbitrary bound, as one early exegete said, and that is why the early exegetes disagreed so much about its measure.

"Fine horses" are those branded with the mark of nobility, "cattle" are the camels and cows, and "fertile land" the cultivated fields and their crops. All of this together is the adornment and pleasure of the worldly life, which is enjoyed for a short while and then passes away. But the home of the Hereafter, the finest destination, is better and more lasting for those who are mindful of Allah, and Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account.

He bestows His bounty upon whom He wills without any reckoning against deeds, out of His grace, so do not let the appeal of this adornment turn you away from what is with your Lord, which neither perishes nor fades, and do not prefer the enjoyment of this world over the enjoyment of the next. The desires enumerated are permissible in themselves, and nothing in them is forbidden, but loving them and preferring them over the Hereafter is what is censured, for the worldly life is a deception and a passing enjoyment, while what is with Allah is abiding and better for those who do right. The believer may enjoy what Allah has made lawful, but he must not let it occupy his heart or become his ultimate concern, for whoever loves the worldly life and its adornment will find it turn against him and leave him with regret, while whoever seeks the pleasure of Allah finds in Him a replacement for everything he gave up. The scholars said the worldly life is like a traveler resting at noon beneath a tree and then moving on, and that the true enjoyers are those who enjoy what is lawful without letting it distract them from the Hereafter, for the Hereafter is better and more lasting, and Allah is the Lord of great bounty, giving provision to whom He wills without account. This is the bounty of Allah, for He is the Lord of great bounty, and His bounty encompasses all His creatures, though He gives extra to whom He wills of His servants out of His grace, so that the abundance some possess is no proof of their nearness to Him and the poverty of others is no proof of His displeasure, for provision and sustenance are in His hand alone, and He enriches and impoverishes whom He wills.

phrases.ar: ۞ قُلۡ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُم بِخَيۡرٖ مِّن ذَٰلِكُمۡۖ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتٞ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزۡوَٰجٞ مُّطَهَّرَةٞ وَرِضۡوَٰنٞ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of what is better than ˹all of˺ this? Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will have Gardens with their Lord under which rivers flow, to stay there forever, and pure spouses, along with Allah’s pleasure.” And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation:
"Say, shall I tell you of something better than this for those who fear their Lord: Gardens under which rivers flow, where they will stay forever, pure spouses, and the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of His servants." Say, O Prophet, to the people for whom the love of women, sons, and the rest has been made fair-seeming: shall I inform you of something better? For the God-fearing there are, with their Lord, gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding forever, purified spouses, and the good pleasure of Allah.

The grammarians differed over where the question ends: some said at "something better than this," so the gardens are a new statement about the God-fearing, and the correct view is that one, because the gardens belong to those who fear their Lord, and Allah is All-Seeing of His servants, knowing who among them truly fears Him.

phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.translation: who pray, “Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
phrases.explanation: "Those who say, Our Lord, we truly believe, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." These are those the question refers to: the God-fearing, who say: we have believed in You, in Your Prophet, and in what he brought. "So forgive us our sins" means pardon and cover them. "And protect us from the torment of the Fire" was singled out because whoever is kept from the Fire attains deliverance. "Protect" comes from "Allah has protected someone," meaning He turned harm away. The grammarians noted "those who say" can be genitive, referring back to the God-fearing, or nominative as a new sentence.

phrases.ar: ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلۡمُنفِقِينَ
phrases.translation: ˹It is they˺ who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable,
phrases.explanation: "It is they who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable." "The patient" are those who showed patience in adversity and hardship and at the moment of battle. "The sincere" are those who were truthful toward Allah in their word, by affirming their acknowledgment of Him, of His Messenger, and of what He brought from Him, and by acting on what He commanded them and avoiding what He forbade them. "The obedient" are those who are obedient to Him in all their affairs. "The charitable" are those who give the obligatory alms on their possessions and dispense them as Allah commanded, and those who spend their wealth in the ways in which Allah loves to see spending.

phrases.ar: وَٱلۡمُسۡتَغۡفِرِينَ بِٱلۡأَسۡحَارِ
phrases.translation: and who pray for forgiveness before dawn
phrases.explanation: And who pray for forgiveness before dawn. "Before dawn" means in the last hours of the night, the plural of the last part of the night before dawn. The clearest of its meanings is that their asking Him for forgiveness takes place by supplication in those hours, when supplications are answered and the gates of mercy are opened. It is also possible that its meaning is their striving for His forgiveness by means of righteous deeds and night prayer and rising at that time, for whoever rises in the last part of the night to pray and ask pardon is among those whom Allah praises. All these words stand in the genitive referring back to "those who say, Our Lord, we truly believe," and together they complete the description of the people of Paradise. The commentator noted that these qualities, patience, sincerity, obedience, charity, and seeking forgiveness at dawn, are the traits of those whom Allah mentioned as inheriting Paradise, and that each of them was explained in detail earlier in the commentary with the reports supporting it.

phrases.ar: شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ
phrases.translation: Allah ˹Himself˺ is a Witness that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—and so are the angels and people of knowledge.
phrases.explanation:
"Allah Himself is a Witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Him, and so are the angels and people of knowledge. He is the Maintainer of justice." Allah has borne witness that there is no god but He, and the angels have borne witness, and those who possess knowledge, upholding justice.

The reciters of the people of Islam read it with a fatha on the first "that He," governed by the verb "bears witness," and a kasra on the second "there is no god." Some scholars of Basra explained "Allah bears witness" as "Allah has decreed," reading the angels in the nominative, but that belongs to what is not known in the language of the Arabs, and the correct view is the first reading, confirmed by the consensus of the reciters. "Upholding justice" stands in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, and the grammarians differed whether it qualifies "He" in "there is no god except Him" or the name Allah in "Allah bears witness," the more correct being that it qualifies Allah, who upholds justice with His servants.

Allah intended this verse to deny what the Christians, who disputed with the Messenger concerning the son of Mary, ascribed to Him of sonship, and what all the rest of the rejectors ascribed to Him of partners. The aim of the statement is the report of the witnessing of those of His creatures whom He chose and who declared His oneness, namely His angels and the learned among His servants, with the mention of Allah and His qualification inserted as a parenthetical, as happens in other verses of the Book.

phrases.ar: أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ قَآئِمَۢا بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
phrases.translation: He is the Maintainer of justice. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Almighty, All-Wise." This denies that anything at all deserves worship apart from the One who has no partner in His divinity. "The Almighty" is the One for whom nothing He wills is impossible, and whom no one can resist or repel when He punishes or takes vengeance upon His enemies. "The All-Wise" is the One who is wise in His disposing of all affairs and in His legislation, so that nothing in His creation is in vain and no soul is wronged. This testimony of Allah, His angels, and the people of knowledge is the firmest proof of His oneness, and it settles the dispute of those who claimed a son or partners for Him.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمُۗ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡعِلۡمُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۗ وَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
phrases.translation: Certainly, Allah’s only Way is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture did not dispute ˹among themselves˺ out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them. Whoever denies Allah’s signs, then surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation:
"Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam." The word "religion" here means obedience and submission, as the poets used it when they spoke of people being brought low into submission by humiliation, and of one humbling another time after time by raid and assault, and of a woman humbling those who were averse to submission.

So Allah says the only obedience and submission acceptable to Him is Islam, the religion He chose for His servants and legislated for them. He sent it through His final Messenger and abrogated what came before it, and He made it the seal of all religions. Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam will never have it accepted from him, and he will be among the losers on the Day of Resurrection, for nothing is accepted from anyone except what He has legislated, and He legislated Islam alone. This verse answers the Christians who disputed about the son of Mary and claimed other than Islam, affirming that the only path with Him is submission to Him alone. The exegetes agreed that "religion" in this verse is obedience and submission, and they cited poetry in which submission meant humiliation and being brought low, to show that the word carries the sense of yielding and humbling oneself before Allah, which is the essence of Islam, the religion of all the prophets from the first to the last.

phrases.ar: فَإِنۡ حَآجُّوكَ فَقُلۡ أَسۡلَمۡتُ وَجۡهِيَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِۗ وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ ءَأَسۡلَمۡتُمۡۚ فَإِنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْ فَقَدِ ٱهۡتَدَواْۖ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَلَٰغُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.translation: So if they argue with you ˹O Prophet˺, say, “I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have my followers.” And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate ˹people˺, “Have you submitted yourselves ˹to Allah˺?” If they submit, they will be ˹rightly˺ guided. But if they turn away, then your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺. And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation:
"And if they dispute with you, then say: I have submitted my face to Allah, and so has whoever follows me." If the Christians of Najran dispute with you, O Prophet, about the son of Mary, say: I have submitted my whole self to Allah, in sincerity of heart and inward submission, not merely outward compliance.

"And whoever follows me" means whoever follows me has likewise submitted his face to Allah with me. And say to those given the Book and to the unlettered: have you submitted? If they submit, they are rightly guided. If they turn away, say: I have warned you, and Allah knows what you conceal. The question form carries the force of a command, as happens elsewhere in the Book, and the exegetes explained it likewise, answering the objection that a question may carry the full import of an order.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
phrases.translation: Indeed, those who deny Allah’s signs, kill the prophets unjustly, and kill people who stand up for justice—give them good news of a painful punishment
phrases.explanation:
"Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right, and kill those who enjoin justice among people, give them tidings of a painful punishment." "Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah" are those who deny Allah's proofs and dismiss them as falsehood, among the Jews and others. "And kill the prophets without right" means they killed the messengers sent to them with the truth and with the prohibition of disobedience. "And kill those who enjoin justice among the people" refers to those who command fairness and equity and forbid oppression.

The reciters differed: the majority of Medina, Hijaz, Basra, Kufa, and the other cities read "and they kill those who enjoin justice," while some later reciters of Kufa read "and they fight," relying on a reading attributed to a companion. The correct reading is "and they kill," by the consensus of the authoritative reciters. Give them tidings of a painful punishment, for what they did will not be left unanswered, and their killing of the prophets and the men of justice is among the gravest of crimes. Allah mentioned these three things together because they are the foundations of corruption in the earth: denying His signs, killing His prophets, and killing those who enjoin justice, for whoever does these has severed himself from the covenant of Allah and will meet a painful punishment in this world and the next.

phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَبِطَتۡ أَعۡمَٰلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
phrases.translation: They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter. And they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation:
"They are those whose works have come to nothing in this world and in the Hereafter, and they have no helpers." "They" refers to those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. Their works have come to nothing in this world and the next, because disbelief nullifies whatever good they did, and their deeds rise to nothing on the Day of Resurrection.

"And they have no helpers" means no one will help them against Allah when He takes vengeance upon them for their crimes and their insolence toward His messengers, for the helper of a wrongdoer is of no avail when the punishment of Allah descends upon him.

phrases.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيبٗا مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّىٰ فَرِيقٞ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَهُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
phrases.translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures? Yet when they are invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes, some of them turn away heedlessly
phrases.explanation: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They are called to the Book of Allah, that it may judge between them, and then a group of them turns away while they are averse." "Those given a portion of the Book" are those given a share of the Scripture, the Jews. They are called to the Book of Allah that it may judge between them. The exegetes differed over which Book: some said the Torah, which they acknowledged, others said the Book sent to the Prophet, to whom a group were called that he might judge between them, but they refused and turned away averse, because of their disbelief in what was sent to him.

phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ لَن تَمَسَّنَا ٱلنَّارُ إِلَّآ أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۖ وَغَرَّهُمۡ فِي دِينِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
phrases.translation: This is because they say, “The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.” They have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying
phrases.explanation:
"That is because they said: The Fire will only touch us for a counted number of days, and what they used to invent has deluded them in their religion." "Because they said" explains the "because" in the verse: these people, summoned to the Book of Allah to judge justly between them, turned away, and the reason was their saying that the Fire will touch them only for a few counted days, a saying explained earlier at the head of the second chapter.

What they fabricated and invented about their religion has deluded them, for they thought their lineage or their book exempted them from punishment, and the oath-discharging notion behind their claim was a false absolution. So they turned away from the Book of Allah while averse, and their fabrication deceived them.

phrases.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جَمَعۡنَٰهُمۡ لِيَوۡمٖ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ وَوُفِّيَتۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: But how ˹horrible˺ will it be when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt—when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation:
"How will it be, then, when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged?" "How will it be" means in what state will these people be when Allah gathers them for the Day of reckoning. How tremendous will be the punishment they shall undergo.

"About which there is no doubt" means there is no doubt about its coming. "Paid in full to every soul what it has earned" means Allah repays each soul for its good and evil, "and they will not be wronged," not even by the weight of an atom.

phrases.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ مَٰلِكَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ تُؤۡتِي ٱلۡمُلۡكَ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَنزِعُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ مِمَّن تَشَآءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَآءُۖ بِيَدِكَ ٱلۡخَيۡرُۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Allah! Lord over all authorities! You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please; You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please—all good is in Your Hands. Surely You ˹alone˺ are Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation:
"Say: O Allah, Owner of all sovereignty, You grant sovereignty to whom You will and take sovereignty from whom You will. You honor whom You will and humiliate whom You will. In Your hand is all good. You make the night pass into the day and the day into the night, You bring the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account."

"Say, O Allah" means say, O Prophet: O Allah. The philologists differed over the accusative of the final letter in this vocative, some saying the rule for a vocative is different here, others saying the Arabs also call it with the vocative particle just as without it, and that the letter was lightened in some dialects. The Prophet used to say in his supplication: O You who turn the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.

"Owner of all sovereignty": sovereignty belongs to Allah, He grants it to whom He wills and removes it from whom He wills, honors whom He wills and humbles whom He wills, for in His hand is all good, and no one can repel His decree.

phrases.ar: تُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِۖ وَتُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ وَتُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَيِّۖ وَتَرۡزُقُ مَن تَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٖ
phrases.translation: You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night. You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. And You provide for whoever You will without limit.”
phrases.explanation:
"You make the night pass into the day and You make the day pass into the night." "You make pass" means You make enter. He makes what He has shortened from the hours of the night enter into the hours of the day, adding to the day by the diminution of the night, and likewise the reverse, so that day and night alternate in turn for the rest of people by night and their seeking of livelihood by day.

"You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living." The exegetes differed over this: some said He brings the living creature out of the dead sperm-drop, and brings the dead sperm-drop out of the living creature, meaning the origin of creation in the womb. Others understood it of the resurrection, when the living will be brought out of the graves, and of the emergence of the believer from among the disbelievers and the disbeliever from among the believers, for faith and disbelief pass from one to the other in this world. Both meanings return to the same point: life and death, and guidance and misguidance, are in His hand alone, and none brings forth anything except by His permission.

"And You provide for whom You will without account": provision and sustenance are in His hand, and He gives to whom He wills without any reckoning or measure, for He is the Provider, the Generous, and His bounty is vast. The reciters and exegetes agreed on the alternation of night and day as a sign of His power, for the sun and moon run by His command, and whoever reflects upon their alternation knows that their Lord is able to do all things and provides for whom He wills.

phrases.ar: لَّا يَتَّخِذِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۖ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَيۡسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِي شَيۡءٍ إِلَّآ أَن تَتَّقُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ تُقَىٰةٗۗ وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسَهُۥۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
phrases.translation: Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers—and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah—unless it is a precaution against their tyranny. And Allah warns you about Himself. And to Allah is the final return
phrases.explanation:
"The believers must not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Whoever does so has nothing to do with Allah, unless it be taking precaution against them." This is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against taking the unbelievers as helpers, allies, and supporters, clinging to them in their religion, assisting them against the Muslims in place of the believers, and inclining toward them.

"Unless it be taking precaution against them" means except that you guard yourselves against them out of fear, showing them outward friendship and support while inwardly you remain with the believers and do not truly ally with them. The exegetes differed over the meaning of the precaution: some said it means kinship between you and them, but the commentator held that this is not what the outward meaning of the verse indicates. The correct meaning is dissimulation out of fear of their harm, and whoever truly takes them as allies in their religion has nothing to do with Allah, for Allah has no part in that. The exegetes also differed over whether alliance with them is forbidden absolutely or only when it is out of love of their religion, and the outward meaning of the verse forbids taking them as allies in place of the believers in every case, with the exception only of precaution out of fear, which is not true alliance but self-protection.

phrases.ar: قُلۡ إِن تُخۡفُواْ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ أَوۡ تُبۡدُوهُ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, it is known to Allah. For He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Most Capable of everything.”
phrases.explanation:
"Say: Whether you hide what is in your hearts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And Allah is Most Capable of all things." Say, O Prophet, to those whom you commanded not to take the unbelievers as allies: whether you conceal what is in your hearts of loyalty to them or reveal it openly, Allah knows it, for nothing is hidden from Him in the heavens or on the earth.

"And Allah is Most Capable of all things": He has the power to punish you swiftly for your loyalty to them and your support of them against the believers, so fear Him and turn to Him.

phrases.ar: يَوۡمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ مِنۡ خَيۡرٖ مُّحۡضَرٗا وَمَا عَمِلَتۡ مِن سُوٓءٖ تَوَدُّ لَوۡ أَنَّ بَيۡنَهَا وَبَيۡنَهُۥٓ أَمَدَۢا بَعِيدٗاۗ وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسَهُۥۗ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.translation: ˹Watch for˺ the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done. And it will wish that its misdeeds were far off. And Allah warns you about Himself. And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants
phrases.explanation: "On the Day when every soul will find the good it has done presented before it, and whatever evil it has done, it will wish there were a great distance between it and that evil. And Allah warns you of Himself. And Allah is Kind to His servants." On that Day every soul finds the good it did present and fully brought forth, and the evil it did it wishes were at a great distance from it. "And Allah warns you of Himself" means He cautions you against His punishment. "And Allah is Kind to His servants" means He is merciful, accepting repentance and pardoning sins, and warning His servants of Himself so that they fear Him and return to Him.

phrases.ar: قُلۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي يُحۡبِبۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If you ˹sincerely˺ love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive your sins. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation:
"Say: If you truly love Allah, then follow me, and Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." The exegetes differed over the occasion of this verse: some said it was revealed about a people in the time of the Prophet who claimed to love Allah but did not follow him, while others said it is a command from Allah to His Prophet to say to the delegation of Najran, who claimed love for the son of Mary contrary to what Allah legislated.

In either case the meaning is the same: love for Allah is proven only by following His Messenger, and whoever follows him, Allah loves him and forgives him his sins, for He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

phrases.ar: قُلۡ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَۖ فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Obey Allah and His Messenger.” If they still turn away, then truly Allah does not like the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: "Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers." Say, O Prophet, to the delegation of the Christians of Najran: obey Allah and the Messenger, for you have known with certainty the truth of what he brought and the proofs he presented. If they obey, they are rightly guided and will attain what Allah has promised the believers. If they turn away, make known to them that Allah does not love whoever disbelieves, denying what he has recognized, and that they are among those who turn away from the truth after it became clear to them, and there is no excuse left for them in what they denied.

phrases.ar: ۞ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحٗا وَءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَءَالَ عِمۡرَٰنَ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ’Imrân above all people ˹of their time˺
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran above all people." Allah selected Adam and Noah on account of their religion and their prophethood, and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran likewise on account of their religion, above all the worlds, meaning above all mankind and the jinn, whom He created in their multitudes. By "family" He meant the followers of the man, his people, and whoever is upon his religion, as was demonstrated earlier, and by the two families He meant only the believers among them, for the disbelievers of a prophet's family are not included in his chosen family.

phrases.ar: ذُرِّيَّةَۢ بَعۡضُهَا مِنۢ بَعۡضٖۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
phrases.translation: They are descendants of one another. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: "A progeny, one part of it descended from the other. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." Allah chose the house of Abraham and the house of Imran as a progeny, one part descending from the other, generation after generation, in an unbroken line of prophethood and guidance. The word "progeny" stands in the accusative as a specification of what was chosen, or as a repetition of "He chose." "One part from the other" was said with regard to their mutual alliance in religion and their mutual support in Islam and the truth, for the chosen of every age are linked to one another by faith. And Allah is All-Hearing of all speech and All-Knowing of all that is hidden.

phrases.ar: إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ عِمۡرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطۡنِي مُحَرَّرٗا فَتَقَبَّلۡ مِنِّيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when the wife of ’Imrân said, “My Lord! I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service, so accept it from me. You ˹alone˺ are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”
phrases.explanation: "When the wife of Imran said: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated to Your service, so accept it from me. You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." The wife of Imran is the mother of Mary, daughter of Imran and mother of the son of Mary. Her name was Hannah according to what has been reported, and her husband Imran was of the lineage of the prophets. "I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated" means she made a vow that what was in her womb belonged to the service of Allah, set free from worldly concerns, and she asked Him to accept it, calling on His names the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing.

phrases.ar: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتۡهَا قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعۡتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتۡ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلۡأُنثَىٰۖ وَإِنِّي سَمَّيۡتُهَا مَرۡيَمَ وَإِنِّيٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
phrases.translation: When she delivered, she said, “My Lord! I have given birth to a girl,”—and Allah fully knew what she had delivered—“and the male is not like the female. I have named her Mary, and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed.”
phrases.explanation:
"So when she gave birth to her, she said: My Lord, I gave birth to a female, and Allah knows best what she bore. The male is not like the female. I have named her Mary. And I seek the protection of Allah for her and her offspring from the accursed Satan." When Hannah gave birth to the one she had vowed, she said she had borne a female, and Allah knows best what she bore, for He is the Knower of the unseen and He decrees what He wills. The reciters differed over the reading of "she bore," most reading it as a report from Allah about Himself, others reading it differently, and the grammar of the verse supports the majority reading.

"The male is not like the female" in this service, for the vowed service in the temple of the Children of Israel was for a male, and she apologized to her Lord for the female, while affirming that Allah knows best what suits His service. She named her Mary, a noble name, and asked Allah to protect her and her offspring from the rejected Satan, and Allah accepted her vow and made Mary the best of women.

phrases.ar: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٖ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنٗا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّاۖ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيۡهَا زَكَرِيَّا
phrases.translation: So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing—entrusting her to the care of Zachariah.
phrases.explanation:
"So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing, entrusting her to the care of Zachariah." Allah accepted Mary from her mother Hannah together with the vow she had made, with a goodly acceptance, for "acceptance" is the verbal noun of "her Lord accepted her," and the grammarians noted that the Arabs inflect this word unusually. And He made her grow with a goodly growth in her nourishment, her sustenance, and her upbringing.

"And He made Zachariah her guardian." The reciters differed over this word: most of the reciters of Hijaz, Medina, and Basra read it with a light letter, meaning Zachariah took her to himself, while most of the reciters of Kufa read it with doubling, meaning Allah made Zachariah her guardian. The correct reading is the doubling, because Allah assigned her to Zachariah over his opponents, and the people of the temple cast lots for her guardianship. The exegetes differed over how the lots were cast: some said Zachariah's shaft rose up in the river while the others drifted with the current, and others said the shafts went along with the water and his alone remained, and in either case it was a decree of Allah by which He gave her to Zachariah. The other reading is supported by another verse, "which of them would be guardian of Mary," but that does not preclude a man appointing another as guardian and that other taking guardianship. The exegetes agreed that the guardianship of Mary was by the decree of Allah, and they reported that the priests of the temple cast lots for her, writing their names on shafts and casting them into the water, and the sign was that Zachariah's shaft remained while the others drifted, or that his rose up in the river, according to the two reports. Whichever it was, there is no doubt it was a decree of Allah assigning her to Zachariah over his opponents. The acceptance of her vow meant that her dedication to the service of the temple was accepted, and she was set apart for worship and for nearness to Allah in the sanctuary, under the care of a prophet, and her upbringing was blessed in religion and character, so that she grew up chaste, modest, and devoted, a model for the women of her time and an argument for her Lord's power over His servants, and a demonstration that He raises whom He wills by His grace, and that the vow of a sincere servant is accepted and honored.

phrases.ar: ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزۡقٗاۖ قَالَ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَاۖ قَالَتۡ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٍ
phrases.translation: Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary, he found her supplied with provisions. He exclaimed, “O Mary! Where did this come from?” She replied, “It is from Allah. Surely Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.”
phrases.explanation: "Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary, he found her supplied with provisions. He exclaimed, O Mary, where did this come from? She replied: It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account." This happened when Zachariah saw with Mary what he saw of provision brought to her in the sanctuary without any human hand, for Allah provides whom He wills without reckoning. He asked her where it came from, and she answered that it was from Allah. This was a sign of her honor and of the acceptance of her mother's vow, and it strengthened Zachariah's hope for offspring in his old age.

phrases.ar: هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبۡ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةٗ طَيِّبَةًۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
phrases.translation: Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring. You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”
phrases.explanation: "Then Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying: My Lord, grant me by Your grace righteous offspring. You are certainly the Hearer of all prayers." Zachariah called upon his Lord at that moment, when he saw with Mary what he saw of provision, for the family of his house had died out and he had no heir, and he was an old man whose wife was barren. "Offspring" means descendants, and "righteous offspring" means blessed, upright descendants. "From Your presence" means from with You, in Your nearness, and "by Your grace" is tied to it. "You are the Hearer of all prayers": He hears every supplication, for He is All-Hearing, and He answers whom He wills, so the prayer of an old man is not cut off from Him, and He grants the righteous a goodly offspring.

phrases.ar: فَنَادَتۡهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآئِمٞ يُصَلِّي فِي ٱلۡمِحۡرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحۡيَىٰ مُصَدِّقَۢا بِكَلِمَةٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَسَيِّدٗا
phrases.translation: So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary,
phrases.explanation:
"So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary: Allah gives you good news of the birth of John, who will confirm the Word of Allah and will be a great leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous." The reciters differed over "the angels called": the general body of the reciters of Medina and some of Kufa and Basra read it in the feminine plural, "the angels called to him," while a group of Kufa read it in the masculine, "then Gabriel called to him," putting the verb in the masculine on account of Gabriel, and some interpreters likewise explained it as Gabriel speaking to him face to face.

The glad tidings was the birth of a son to Zachariah in his old age, for Allah gives whom He wills offspring even when age and barrenness make it seem impossible. The glad tidings came to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary, in the place of prostration, showing that supplication in the sacred place is answered, and that the servant should turn to his Lord in his need and ask Him with hope, for Allah is the Hearer of all prayers and gives whom He wills a righteous offspring.

phrases.ar: وَحَصُورٗا وَنَبِيّٗا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
phrases.translation: “Allah gives you good news of ˹the birth of˺ John who will confirm the Word of Allah and will be a great leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: "John, who will confirm the Word of Allah and will be a great leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous." John will confirm a word from Allah, that is the son of Mary, believing in him and testifying to his truth, for he was sent before him as a witness. He will be a great leader, honored among his people, chaste, refraining from women and desire, and a prophet among the righteous, one of the best of the Children of Israel. Allah chose him for prophethood and for these qualities before his birth, and He gave his father the glad tidings of him while he stood praying in the sanctuary. The exegetes noted that John was given prophethood while young and was described with all these qualities, and that the glad tidings of such a son is a mercy from Allah to His servant, a reason for the believer to hope in Allah's bounty and to ask Him for righteous offspring, and to accept what He decrees for him.

phrases.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَٰمٞ وَقَدۡ بَلَغَنِيَ ٱلۡكِبَرُ وَٱمۡرَأَتِي عَاقِرٞۖ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱللَّهُ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ
phrases.translation: Zachariah exclaimed, “My Lord! How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren?” He replied, “So will it be. Allah does what He wills.”
phrases.explanation: "Zachariah exclaimed: My Lord, how can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren? He replied: So will it be. Allah does what He wills." Zachariah said this when the angels called to him with the glad tidings: how can I have a son when old age has reached me and my wife is barren. "Barren" is she who does not bear children, and it applies to a woman and a man. "Old age" is the verbal noun of growing old, and what reaches you, you have also reached. The angel replied: so will it be, for Allah does what He wills, and nothing is impossible for Him.

phrases.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَل لِّيٓ ءَايَةٗۖ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمۡزٗاۗ
phrases.translation: Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.”
phrases.explanation:
"Zachariah said: My Lord, grant me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you will not be able to speak to people for three days except through gestures." Zachariah said: My Lord, make for me a sign, if this call with which I was called and the voice I heard are from You, for I want certainty. "Sign" means a mark, and its meaning was demonstrated earlier, so repetition is unnecessary. The linguists differed over why its hamza is dropped while Arabs usually hamza a letter after a quiescent alif: some said it was originally different and the doubling was burdensome, others that it is a pattern whose first letter became an alif, as with other words, and objections were answered by examples of the language.

Allah gave him the sign: "Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture." The reciters chose the accusative in "that you shall not speak," because the meaning of the utterance is that the sign is your not speaking. According to what has been transmitted, Allah made him dumb for asking for the sign after the glad tidings had reached him, and some exegetes said this too. The sign was a trial for him for asking after the glad tidings, and it was also a mercy, for it occupied him with silence and remembrance for three days, and the exegetes noted that asking for a sign after clear evidence is a shortcoming, though Allah answered him and gave him the sign he asked for, and made the sign itself a means of drawing him closer through remembrance.

phrases.ar: وَٱذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ كَثِيرٗا وَسَبِّحۡ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِبۡكَٰرِ
phrases.translation: He said, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three days except through gestures. Remember your Lord often and glorify ˹Him˺ morning and evening.”
phrases.explanation: "Remember your Lord often and glorify Him morning and evening." "Except by gesture": the predominant meaning of "gesture" among the Arabs is beckoning with the lips, and sometimes with the eyebrows and eyes. So he spoke to people only by sign for three whole days, and in that time he remembered his Lord often and glorified Him morning and evening, for whoever is given a sign of nearness from his Lord should respond with remembrance and glorification, and the three days of silence were a trial that turned into worship. He praised his Lord much in those three days, for glorification at the boundaries of the day is among the most beloved deeds, and he emerged from the silence with increased remembrance and gratitude.

phrases.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَٱصۡطَفَىٰكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when the angels said, “O Mary! Surely Allah has selected you, purified you, and chosen you over all women of the world
phrases.explanation: "And remember when the angels said: O Mary, surely Allah has selected you, purified you, and chosen you over all women of the world." This refers back to the story of the wife of Imran and her vow. "Selected you" means He chose you and singled you out for His obedience and for the honor with which He distinguished you. "Purified you" means He purified your religion of doubt and of the blemishes found in the religions of the women of the children of Adam, as one exegete said. "Chosen you over the women of the worlds" means He preferred you above the women of the worlds in your time, through your obedience to Him, and thus raised you above them all. The angels said this to Mary face to face, as has been mentioned, and the singular pronoun after the comparative refers back to the plural, as occurs in classical Arabic.

phrases.ar: يَٰمَرۡيَمُ ٱقۡنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ وَٱسۡجُدِي وَٱرۡكَعِي مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
phrases.translation: O Mary! Be devout to your Lord, prostrate yourself ˹in prayer˺ and bow along with those who bow down.”
phrases.explanation: "O Mary, be devout to your Lord, prostrate yourself in prayer and bow along with those who bow down." "Be devout to your Lord" means be obedient to Him with prolonged devotion. The exegetes differed over "devout": some said it means prolong the standing in prayer, others that it means humility and lowliness before Allah, and others that it means continuous obedience day and night. All these meanings point to one thing, namely that Mary was singled out to worship her Lord with devotion, prostration, and bowing along with those who bow, and she answered with obedience and worship, unlike the disobedient women around her, and she responded to the call of the angels with worship and submission, so Allah raised her station and made her an example for the worlds. The standing, the prostration, and the bowing are the pillars of prayer, and by them the servant humbles himself before his Lord, and Mary combined them all in her devotion, which is why she was chosen over the women of the worlds.

phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيۡكَۚ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيۡهِمۡ إِذۡ يُلۡقُونَ أَقۡلَٰمَهُمۡ أَيُّهُمۡ يَكۡفُلُ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيۡهِمۡ إِذۡ يَخۡتَصِمُونَ
phrases.translation: This is news of the unseen that We reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺. You were not with them when they cast lots to decide who would be Mary’s guardian, nor were you there when they argued ˹about it˺
phrases.explanation: "This is news of the unseen that We reveal to you, O Prophet. You were not with them when they cast lots to decide who would be Mary's guardian, nor were you there when they argued about it." By "the unseen" He means these are tidings of what was hidden from that people, which you, O Muhammad, did not know, nor did your people, and which We reveal to you as proof of your prophethood and confirmation of your truthfulness. The casting of lots was how the guardianship of Mary was decided among her people: they wrote their names and cast them, and the lot fell to Zachariah. "The unseen" is a verbal noun from absence, for what is absent from sight is hidden. And you were not present with them, nor a witness when they disputed over her guardianship, yet Allah informed you of it, and that is among the signs of a true prophet, for the one whom Allah informs of the unseen is sent with truth. The argument over her guardianship was between her people, and they cast lots for it, and We tell you of it though you were not present, to establish the proof against those who deny you. Allah said this to His Prophet to console him and to show that the story of Mary and the casting of lots belongs to the unseen that He reveals to His messenger. The lots were cast by her people to decide who would take her guardianship, and the dispute arose among them over her, and none of them was worthy except the one Allah chose. You were not present, O Muhammad, yet We narrate it to you exactly, and in that is a sign for those who reflect, for Allah knows the unseen and the seen, and He informs His Prophet of what He wills of the hidden tidings of the past peoples, as He informed you of the stories of the prophets before you.

phrases.ar: إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٖ مِّنۡهُ ٱسۡمُهُ ٱلۡمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ وَجِيهٗا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when the angels proclaimed, “O Mary! Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him, his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary; honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be one of those nearest ˹to Allah˺
phrases.explanation: "Remember when the angels proclaimed: O Mary, Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him, his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be one of those nearest to Allah." "The glad tidings" is informing a person of news that gladdens him. "A Word from Him" means a message and a report from Allah, for He creates by His word: when He decrees a matter, He says to it "Be," and it is. The words mean that you, O Muhammad, were not present with them when the angels gave Mary this glad tidings, yet We reveal it to you. His name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, honored in this world and the Hereafter by prophethood and nearness to Allah, and one of those brought nearest to Him. And the interpreters said that the Word from Him is a spirit and a creation of Allah, and that He named him the Messiah because he was anointed with blessing, and Jesus by the name given to him, and he was honored in this world by the Children of Israel and in the Hereafter by nearness to Allah. It is said that the Word from Him was carried by the spirit who breathed it into her, and that Allah created the son of Mary by His word without a father, to establish His power. He is honored in this world and the Hereafter, for he is among those brought nearest to Allah, and the angels gave Mary this news while she was in the sanctuary, and she believed and submitted, praising her Lord for His favor upon her, and she was patient with what Allah decreed for her, for the believer accepts the decree of his Lord with contentment.

phrases.ar: وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِي ٱلۡمَهۡدِ وَكَهۡلٗا وَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
phrases.translation: And he will speak to people in ˹his˺ infancy and adulthood and will be one of the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: "And he will speak to people in his infancy and adulthood and will be one of the righteous." "Speaks" stands in the nominative because of its form, yet its meaning is that Allah made him speak in the cradle, which was a miracle. "The cradle" is the resting place of the child during nursing. And he will speak to people in adulthood as a prophet calling to Allah. And he will be one of the righteous, for Allah purified him and chose him, and speaking in infancy was among the signs of his prophethood and of the power of Allah over His servants. It is said that he spoke in the cradle to defend his mother's honor and to declare her chastity, which was a clear sign. And his speaking in adulthood would be the speech of a prophet conveying the message, and his being among the righteous is because Allah purified him and chose him from among the children of Adam, so he combined miracle, prophethood, and righteousness.

phrases.ar: قَالَتۡ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدٞ وَلَمۡ يَمۡسَسۡنِي بَشَرٞۖ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ ٱللَّهُ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرٗا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
phrases.translation: Mary wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me?” An angel replied, “So will it be. Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, ‘Be!’ And it is
phrases.explanation: "Mary wondered: My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has ever touched me? An angel replied: So will it be. Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, Be, and it is." Mary said this when the glad tidings reached her: how can I have a child when no man has touched me, for I am chaste. The angel replied: thus does Allah create what He wills, by His word alone, to show His power, and she submitted to the decree of her Lord, and it is said that she conceived by the word of Allah without a mate, as a sign for the people that He creates what He wills.

phrases.ar: وَيُعَلِّمُهُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلَ
phrases.translation: And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel
phrases.explanation: "And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel." The reciters differed: the general reciters of Hijaz, Medina, and some of Kufa read "and He will teach him," while the reciters of Kufa and some of Basra read "and We will teach him," connecting it with what precedes. Either way, the statement is from Allah to Mary about what He would do with the child announced to her: He would teach him the Book, that is the scripture, and wisdom, the understanding and judgment, and the Torah and the Gospel, the two scriptures revealed before, so that he would confirm them and call his people to them, and he would teach them what was in them, for he was taught the Book and wisdom directly, without a teacher.

phrases.ar: وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنِّي قَدۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٖ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ أَنِّيٓ أَخۡلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيۡـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيۡرَۢا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَأُبۡرِئُ ٱلۡأَكۡمَهَ وَٱلۡأَبۡرَصَ وَأُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا تَأۡكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡۚ
phrases.translation: and ˹make him˺ a messenger to the Children of Israel ˹to proclaim,˺ ‘I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I will make for you a bird from clay, breathe into it, and it will become a ˹real˺ bird—by Allah’s Will. I will heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead to life—by Allah’s Will. And I will prophesize what you eat and store in your houses.
phrases.explanation: "And make him a messenger to the Children of Israel to proclaim: I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I will make for you a bird from clay, breathe into it, and it will become a bird by Allah's permission, and I will heal the blind and the leper and revive the dead by His permission, and I will tell you what you eat and what you store in your homes. Surely in that is a sign for you if you are believers." Allah made the son of Mary a messenger to the Children of Israel, and his being the Messiah, born without a father, is itself the sign. "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" means the miracles he would perform: making a bird from clay and breathing into it so it becomes a living bird by Allah's permission, healing the born blind and the leper, reviving the dead by His permission, and telling them what they eat and store in their homes, which is knowledge of the unseen given to him. All of this is by the permission of Allah, for he does nothing of his own accord. In that is a sign for you if you are believers, and the exegetes said the bird from clay was a real bird that flew, and the healing and reviving were signs of his truthfulness. The reciters differed over "in the likeness of the bird": some of Hijaz read it in the singular, "in the likeness of a bird, I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird," while others read it with the plural in both places. The meaning is that he breathed into the clay bird. It was mentioned that when he wished to fashion the bird he asked them which bird was strongest in creation, and was told the bat, and he fashioned birds of various kinds and breathed into them, and they became living birds that flew by Allah's permission. He healed the born blind and the leper, reviving the dead by His permission, and he told them what they ate and stored in their homes, which is knowledge of the unseen that Allah taught him. All his miracles were by the permission of Allah, and in them is a sign for the believers that he was sent from Allah. The exegetes differed over "the one born blind": some said it is the one who cannot see at night but sees by day, others that it is the one whose mother bore him blind, others simply the blind person, and others the one with weak blinking eyes. In any case the healing of the born blind and the leper was a miracle by the permission of Allah, showing that he was sent from Him. And "I will revive the dead by His permission" and "I will tell you what you eat and what you store in your homes" are knowledge of the unseen given to him by Allah, and all of it is a sign for those who believe, for no one can do these things except by the power of Allah. The interpreters said that all these signs were given to him by Allah to confirm his prophethood to the Children of Israel, and that whoever saw them knew he was a messenger, and that the clay bird became a living bird that ate and drank, and the blind regained sight, and the leper was cleansed, and the dead rose, all by the permission of Allah, and nothing of this is possible except for Allah.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةٗ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for you if you ˹truly˺ believe
phrases.explanation: "And surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him alone. This is the Straight Path." The son of Mary said: surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him alone, for He is the Creator of you and of him, and there is no god but He.
