This is the Straight Path, the path of worship and monotheism, and whoever follows it is guided, and whoever turns from it is astray. The exegetes said this call was made after the miracles were shown, and that the Straight Path is the path of monotheism and obedience, with no deviation, and that whoever worships Allah alone and follows His messenger is upon it.

phrases.ar: وَمُصَدِّقٗا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُم بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَجِئۡتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٖ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
phrases.translation: And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me
phrases.explanation: "And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me." "Confirming the Torah" means he believed in it and acted by it. "Legalizing some of what was forbidden" means he made lawful some things the Torah had forbidden, as a facilitation from Allah, for the laws differ by the needs of the peoples. "Be mindful of Allah and obey me": fear Allah and follow me in what I call you to, and do not disobey me, for obedience to the messenger is obedience to Allah.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمۡ فَٱعۡبُدُوهُۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٞ مُّسۡتَقِيمٞ
phrases.translation: Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.’”
phrases.explanation: "Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him alone. This is the Straight Path." The reciters differed over the opening letter: the majority read "Indeed Allah is my Lord" with a kasra, while some read it with a fatha, "that Allah is my Lord," continuing the speech of the son of Mary. Either way the meaning is: Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him alone. This is the Straight Path, upright and clear, with no crookedness in it, and whoever holds fast to it is upon guidance, and whoever worships other than Allah has gone astray from it, and the worship of Allah alone is the straight path.

phrases.ar: ۞ فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنۡهُمُ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ قَالَ مَنۡ أَنصَارِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ ٱلۡحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحۡنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَٱشۡهَدۡ بِأَنَّا مُسۡلِمُونَ
phrases.translation: When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people, he asked, “Who will stand up with me for Allah?” The disciples replied, “We will stand up for Allah. We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we have submitted.”
phrases.explanation: "When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people, he asked: Who will stand up with me for Allah? The disciples replied: We will stand up for Allah. We believe in Allah, and we bear witness that we are Muslims. They prayed: Our Lord, we believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness." "Sensed" means he perceived and noticed the rejection of his prophethood among the Children of Israel, and "disbelief" here means their denial and their plot against him. He asked who would be his helpers with Allah, meaning alongside Allah in calling to Him, for the Arabs use "unto" in the sense of "with" when joining one thing to another. The exegetes disagreed over why he sought help from the disciples: some said it was because those against whom he asked wished to kill him, and he sought helpers against them, while others said it was to strengthen his call and to show that he had supporters. The disciples, his followers, answered: we are your helpers, we believe in Allah and follow you, we bear witness that we are Muslims submitted to Him, and they prayed: our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and follow the messenger, so write us among the witnesses. Allah praised their words and deeds and made their way a model for those who wish to please Him, and they were twelve in number. The disciples were those who believed in him and followed him, and their number was twelve, and their answer shows sincerity of faith and readiness to support the truth even at cost, and their prayer to be written among the witnesses is the prayer of every believer who testifies to the oneness of Allah and the message of His messenger. Allah mentioned their statement in His Book as an example of truthful speech and righteous deed, and the exegetes transmitted that the disciples were sincere in their faith and were promised Paradise for their support of the prophet.

phrases.ar: رَبَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا بِمَآ أَنزَلۡتَ وَٱتَّبَعۡنَا ٱلرَّسُولَ فَٱكۡتُبۡنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
phrases.translation: ˹They prayed to Allah,˺ “Our Lord! We believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness.”
phrases.explanation: "They prayed to Allah: Our Lord, we believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness." This is the prayer of the disciples of the son of Mary, and Allah made known their way so that people might follow it. They believed in what was sent down, the Gospel, and followed the messenger, and asked to be inscribed among the witnesses, those who bear witness to the oneness of Allah and the truth of His messenger. To bear witness is to testify to the oneness of Allah and the truth of His messenger with the tongue, the heart, and the deeds, and that is the rank of those nearest to Allah.

phrases.ar: وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ ٱللَّهُۖ وَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡمَٰكِرِينَ
phrases.translation: And the disbelievers made a plan ˹against Jesus˺, but Allah also planned—and Allah is the best of planners
phrases.explanation: "And the disbelievers made a plan against Jesus, but Allah also planned, and Allah is the best of planners." Their plan was their agreement to ambush the son of Mary and kill him, for he called them to Allah and exposed their disbelief. And Allah's plan against them was that He cast the likeness of the son of Mary upon one of his followers, so they seized and crucified the wrong man, while Allah raised the son of Mary to Himself. Allah is the best of planners, for His plan encompasses theirs, and no scheme avails against His decree, and whoever plots against the messenger of Allah, Allah plots against him.

phrases.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَىٰٓ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَجَاعِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوكَ فَوۡقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Allah said, “O Jesus! I will take you and raise you up to Myself. I will deliver you from those who disbelieve, and elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: "Remember when Allah said: O Jesus, I will take you and raise you up to Myself. I will deliver you from those who disbelieve, and elevate your followers above those who disbelieve until the Day of Judgment." "I will take you" refers to death, and people differed over it: some said it means sleep, others that he was raised alive, and others that he died and was raised in soul. "I will raise you up to Myself" means I will elevate your rank and raise you to heaven. "I will deliver you from those who disbelieve" means I will protect you from their plot to kill you and make you prevail over them. "Elevate your followers above those who disbelieve until the Day of Judgment" means your nation will remain upon truth and superiority until the end, and the exegetes said this refers to the followers of Muhammad as well, for they follow the true teaching of Jesus. The exegetes disagreed over the "taking": some said it means the death that comes to all, and that he was raised after dying, others that he was taken in sleep and raised alive, and the preferred view is that he was raised to Allah bodily, and that what was crucified was a likeness cast upon another. Whatever the case, Allah delivered him from those who disbelieved and made his followers prevail until the Day of Resurrection, when all will return to Allah for judgment. This was said to console the son of Mary and to establish that his matter is with Allah, for He raises whom He wills and delivers whom He wills.

phrases.ar: ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَكُمۡ فِيمَا كُنتُمۡ فِيهِ تَخۡتَلِفُونَ
phrases.translation: Then to Me you will ˹all˺ return, and I will settle all your disputes
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all. They are the fuel of the Fire, like the people of Pharaoh and those before them." Those who disbelieved in the son of Mary will not be helped by their riches or offspring in the least against Allah. They are the companions of the Fire, and their condition is like that of Pharaoh and his people and those before them, who denied their prophets and were destroyed, and their wealth and children did not avail them anything against Allah. They will enter the Fire and remain in it, and their state is a warning to those who deny the messengers.

phrases.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَأُعَذِّبُهُمۡ عَذَابٗا شَدِيدٗا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
phrases.translation: As for those who disbelieve, I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: "As for those who disbelieve, I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers." Allah says to the son of Mary: as for those who disbelieved in you and denied your message, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, and nothing will protect them. And they will have no helpers to aid them against My punishment, for no one can avert the decree of Allah, and whoever disbelieves in Allah and His messenger has no supporter, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater and more lasting than the punishment of this life.

phrases.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمۡ أُجُورَهُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
phrases.translation: And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: "And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers." "Those who believed and did righteous deeds": He means those who believed in Allah and His messenger and performed good works. "He will give them their rewards in full": He will recompense them completely for their deeds, without any of it being diminished. "Allah does not like the wrongdoers": He does not approve of oppression, and the wrongdoer will not prosper, for Allah loves justice and hates injustice, and He will hold the wrongdoer to account for it. The reward in full is Paradise, and the wrongdoers will get their recompense in the Fire.

phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ نَتۡلُوهُ عَلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ وَٱلذِّكۡرِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
phrases.translation: We recite ˹all˺ this to you ˹O Prophet˺ as one of the signs and ˹as˺ a wise reminder
phrases.explanation: "We recite all this to you, O Prophet, as one of the signs and a wise reminder." "That We recite to you" means this story of the son of Mary and his signs is among the signs of your prophethood, O Muhammad, for you recite it though you were not present. "And a wise reminder": the Quran is a wise reminder, with rulings and wisdom in it, and whoever recites it and acts by it is guided, and it reminds the heedless and warns the heedless of the punishment. It is recited to you so that you may convey it to your people and they may reflect upon it.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَۖ خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٖ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
phrases.translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, “Be!” And he was
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, Be, and he was." Allah sent this verse as an argument for His power and the truth of His messenger against those who denied the creation of the son of Mary without a father. The likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam: He created Adam from dust without a father or mother, then said to him "Be," and he was. So the creation of Jesus from a mother alone, by the word of Allah, is no more wondrous than the creation of Adam from dust, and both are by the power of Allah, who creates what He wills.

phrases.ar: ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡمُمۡتَرِينَ
phrases.translation: This is the truth from your Lord, so do not be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation: "This is the truth from your Lord, so do not be one of those who doubt." "The truth from your Lord": what We have told you of the story of the son of Mary is the truth from your Lord, so do not be of those who doubt. "Doubt," "suspicion," and "misgiving" are one and the same, and whoever doubts the truth after it has come to him is among those who go astray, for the truth needs no doubt once its signs are clear, and the one who doubts after certainty has erred. So believe in what has come to you from your Lord and follow it.

phrases.ar: فَمَنۡ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ فَقُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ نَدۡعُ أَبۡنَآءَنَا وَأَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَكُمۡ وَأَنفُسَنَا وَأَنفُسَكُمۡ ثُمَّ نَبۡتَهِلۡ فَنَجۡعَل لَّعۡنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
phrases.translation: Now, whoever disputes with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you, say, “Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves—then let us sincerely invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.”
phrases.explanation: "Now, whoever disputes with you, O Prophet, concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you, say: Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us pray earnestly and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars." "Concerning him" refers to Jesus, though it is also possible it refers to the truth. This was revealed concerning those who disputed with the Prophet about Jesus after knowledge came to him, and the delegation of Najran is mentioned among them. He is commanded to call them to mutual imprecation: gathering the children, the women, and the parties, and praying earnestly and asking Allah to curse the liar.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلۡقَصَصُ ٱلۡحَقُّۚ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
phrases.translation: Certainly, this is the true narrative, and there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah. And indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "Certainly, this is the true narrative, and there is no god worthy of worship except Allah. And indeed, Allah alone is the Almighty, All-Wise." "This is the true narrative": what We have related to you of the story of Jesus is the true account, and there is no god but Allah, for He has no partner. "The Almighty" means the Almighty in His vengeance against whoever disobeys Him, the Possessor of might and power, and "All-Wise" in His management of His creation, so worship Him alone. The story of Jesus is thus the true narrative, established by clear proofs, and whoever denies it denies the truth. He is the One, the Almighty in His kingdom, the All-Wise in His decree.

phrases.ar: فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
phrases.translation: If they turn away, then surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: "If they turn away, then surely Allah has perfect knowledge of the corruptors." "If they turn away" means if those who disputed with you about Jesus turn away from the truth that came to you from your Lord. "Allah is All-Knowing of the corruptters": Allah knows those who disobey their Lord and spread corruption on earth, and He will requite them for it, for nothing is hidden from Him, and turning away from the truth is corruption, and He sees their corruption and their end. He knows their outward and inward, and He will judge between His servants on the Day of Judgment. So let them turn away if they will, for Allah sees them and knows their secret plotting.

phrases.ar: قُلۡ يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ تَعَالَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٖ سَوَآءِۭ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ أَلَّا نَعۡبُدَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَلَا نُشۡرِكَ بِهِۦ شَيۡـٔٗا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعۡضُنَا بَعۡضًا
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but Allah, associate none with Him, nor take one another as lords instead of Allah.” But if
phrases.explanation: "Say, O Prophet: O People of the Book! Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but Allah, associate none with Him, nor take one another as lords besides Allah. But if they turn away, say: Bear witness that we are Muslims." This was revealed, some said, concerning the Jews around Medina, others concerning the delegation of the Christians of Najran who came to dispute with the Prophet. "Come" means draw near. "An equal word" is the just word, common between us and you. The grammarians differed over how "equal" relates to "word": some said it is a qualifier, others that it is a verbal noun in the place of a participle. The common terms are: worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and take no lords besides Him by obeying one another against Allah. If they accept, well and good, and if they turn away, say: bear witness that we are Muslims, submitted to Allah alone. The exegetes differed over who was addressed: some said the Jews of Medina, others the Christian delegation of Najran. "Common terms" is what both parties agree upon, and the first of them is the worship of Allah alone, for He is the Lord of both parties, and associating partners with Him is the greatest wrong. Taking one another as lords besides Allah means obeying some people in disobedience to Allah, and that is a form of associating partners with Him, for obedience in sin is worship of the obedient one.

phrases.ar: أَرۡبَابٗا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَقُولُواْ ٱشۡهَدُواْ بِأَنَّا مُسۡلِمُونَ
phrases.translation: they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we have submitted ˹to Allah alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: "Say: Bear witness that we are Muslims." If the People of the Book turn away from the common word, then bear witness, O Muslims, that you are submitted to Allah, worshipping Him alone, so that your witness stands against their turning away, and your submission is clear to all, and your testimony will be recorded for you on the Day of Judgment. Say it openly and clearly, and let every party bear witness to its own stance, for the truth will prevail in the end. Do not grieve over their turning away, for guidance is in the hand of Allah, and He guides whom He wills. And Allah is witness over all things.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِيٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَتِ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةُ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him? Do you not understand
phrases.explanation: "O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him? Do you not understand?" Their dispute about Abraham was that each group, the Jews and the Christians, claimed he belonged to them and professed their religion, though the Torah and the Gospel came after him, so how could he follow books revealed after his time. "Do you not understand": do you not use your reason, for this argument is false, and Abraham was upon the pure monotheism before the books, and he called to the worship of Allah alone. So their argument is vain, and reason rejects it.

phrases.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ حَٰجَجۡتُمۡ فِيمَا لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمٞ فَلِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِيمَا لَيۡسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمٞۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: Here you are! You disputed about what you have ˹little˺ knowledge of, but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of? Allah knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: "Here you are! You disputed about what you have little knowledge of, but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of? Allah knows and you do not know." "Here you are": this is an address of reproach. You argued about what you had some knowledge of, namely the matters of your own books, so why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of, namely the story of Jesus and the unseen, which was only revealed to your prophet. Allah knows all things and you know nothing except what He teaches you, so turn back to what He has revealed and do not dispute without knowledge.

phrases.ar: مَا كَانَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ يَهُودِيّٗا وَلَا نَصۡرَانِيّٗا وَلَٰكِن كَانَ حَنِيفٗا مُّسۡلِمٗا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
phrases.translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian; he submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist
phrases.explanation: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian and he submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist." Allah says: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and he was not among the polytheists who worship idols and fire. Rather he was upright, inclined to the pure monotheism, and a Muslim, submitted to Allah alone, the first of the monotheists. So those who claim him for their religions are wrong, for he was upon the straight religion before the Torah and the Gospel, and he called to the worship of Allah alone. He was the first to submit to Allah, and his religion was Islam, pure and true.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ أَوۡلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَٰذَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
phrases.translation: Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet, and the believers. And Allah is the Guardian of those who believe
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet, and the believers. And Allah is the Guardian of those who believe." "The closest of people to Abraham" means those nearest to him in following his religion: those who followed him, and this Prophet Muhammad, and those who believed with him, for they are upon his way. "Allah is the Guardian of the believers": He protects them, helps them, and guides them, for He is their guardian and supporter against their enemies, and whoever has Allah as guardian has no need of others, and He suffices His believing servant. The believers are his party, and his followers inherit his claim.

phrases.ar: وَدَّت طَّآئِفَةٞ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَوۡ يُضِلُّونَكُمۡ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
phrases.translation: Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you ˹believers˺. They mislead none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it
phrases.explanation: "Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you, believers. They mislead none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it." A group of the People of the Book wished to lead the believers astray from their religion. "Leading astray" here means destruction, for those who are led astray from the truth are destroyed. "They mislead none but themselves": their plotting returns upon them, and they harm only their own souls. "Yet they fail to perceive it": they do not realize that their scheming harms them, for they are deluded. Their wish is vain, for Allah protects the believers from their plots. And it is said that their misleading was by their saying that the Quran is not from Allah.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَنتُمۡ تَشۡهَدُونَ
phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you reject the signs of Allah while you bear witness ˹to their truth˺
phrases.explanation: "O People of the Book! Why do you reject the signs of Allah while you bear witness to their truth?" Allah rebukes the People of the Book for their disbelief in Muhammad while they witness to the truth of what came to them, for their own books foretold him and they recognized him by his description. To reject the signs of Allah while bearing witness to their truth is stubbornness, and whoever rejects the truth after recognizing it is upon clear loss, and Allah sees their rejection. They knew the signs in their books yet rejected them out of envy and pride. Turn back to Him, for He is the Oft-Returning.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تَلۡبِسُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتَكۡتُمُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you mix the truth with falsehood and hide the truth knowingly
phrases.explanation: "O People of the Book! Why do you mix the truth with falsehood and hide the truth knowingly?" Their cloaking of the truth with falsehood was that they affirmed with their tongues what they knew of the Prophet while hiding the truth in their hearts and concealing the description they found in their books. "Hide the truth knowingly": you conceal what you know to be true, and that is a great wrong, for whoever hides the truth after knowing it is a witness against himself. Do not hide what you know, for Allah encompasses what you conceal and will bring it to light. Mixing truth with falsehood is a deception that Allah has exposed in His Book so that the believers may beware of it. The People of the Book knew the description of the Prophet in the Torah and the Gospel, yet they concealed it, and concealing the truth after knowing it is a greater sin than denying it in ignorance.

phrases.ar: وَقَالَت طَّآئِفَةٞ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ ءَامِنُواْ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَجۡهَ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱكۡفُرُوٓاْ ءَاخِرَهُۥ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
phrases.translation: A group among the People of the Book said ˹to one another˺, “Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning and reject it in the evening, so they may abandon their faith
phrases.explanation: "A group among the People of the Book said to one another: Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning and reject it in the evening, so that they may turn back." Some of the People of the Book advised one another to show belief in what was revealed to the Muslims at the start of the day and then disavow it at the end, so that the Muslims would doubt their religion and turn back from it. Some said this was a command they gave to each other to deceive the believers, and others explained it differently, but the aim was to cast doubt upon Islam. Allah exposed their scheme and informed His Prophet of it, for He knows what they conceal.

phrases.ar: وَلَا تُؤۡمِنُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمۡ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ أَن يُؤۡتَىٰٓ أَحَدٞ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمۡ أَوۡ يُحَآجُّوكُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّكُمۡۗ
phrases.translation: And only believe those who follow your religion.”
phrases.explanation: "And only believe those who follow your religion. Say, O Prophet: Surely, the only true guidance is Allah's guidance." Allah reports the saying of a group of the People of the Book who advised one another: believe only in him who follows your religion, and do not believe in the religion of Muhammad. So Allah commanded His Prophet to answer them: surely the only true guidance is the guidance of Allah, and whoever is guided by other than Him is astray. Guidance is from Allah alone, and He guides whom He wills to Islam, and no one else has any guidance to give. The People of the Book claimed that only their religion is accepted, and they forbade the believers from believing in Islam, but the answer is that guidance is from Allah alone, and He gives it to whom He wills among His servants. Whoever follows the guidance of Allah is guided, and whoever follows other than it has gone astray, and the People of the Book knew that Islam is the truth yet they concealed it out of envy.

phrases.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡفَضۡلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٞ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely, ˹the only˺ true guidance is Allah’s guidance.” ˹They also said,˺ “Do not believe that someone will receive ˹revealed˺ knowledge similar to yours or argue against you before your Lord.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, all bounty is in the Hands of Allah—He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.”
phrases.explanation: "They also said: Do not tell the believers about what you find in your Book of the description of Muhammad, lest they believe in him and leave your religion. But if you do tell them, deny it. Say: Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." They also advised one another to conceal from the believers what their Book contains of the glad tidings of the Prophet, lest they believe in him. And if they revealed it, to deny it. Allah exposed their scheme and commanded the Prophet to reply: indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, those who conceal the truth and plot against the believers, for He guides only those who follow the truth.

phrases.ar: يَخۡتَصُّ بِرَحۡمَتِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
phrases.translation: He chooses whoever He wills to receive His mercy. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty
phrases.explanation: "He chooses whoever He wills to receive His mercy. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty." "His mercy" in this place means Islam, the Quran, and prophethood together. He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and He withholds it from whom He wills, for bounty is in His hand, and He gives it to whom He wills. "Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty": His favor is great and encompassing, and He bestows it upon His servants according to His wisdom. And the bounty of Allah is vast, for He is the Possessor of the great favor. He does not wrong anyone, for He gives bounty to whom He wills by His wisdom and justice.

phrases.ar: ۞ وَمِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِقِنطَارٖ يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِدِينَارٖ لَّا يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ قَآئِمٗاۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡنَا فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ سَبِيلٞ
phrases.translation: There are some among the People of the Book who, if entrusted with a stack of gold, will readily return it. Yet there are others who, if entrusted with a single coin, will not repay it unless you constantly demand it.
phrases.explanation: "There are some among the People of the Book who, if entrusted with a stack of gold, will readily return it. Yet there are others who, if entrusted with a single coin, will not return it unless you are standing over them, watching. That is because they say: We are not accountable for the gentiles." Of the People of the Book are some who are trustworthy and will return a great treasure if you entrust it to them, and others who are treacherous and will not return even a small amount unless you keep watch over them. Their excuse was that they said there is no accountability upon them concerning the gentiles, meaning they may wrong the unbelievers, but Allah refuted them: surely the covenant of Allah and the oath they took bind them, and betrayal of trust is forbidden to every Muslim against everyone. The trustworthy among them return what is entrusted even if it is great, because they fear Allah and honor the trust, while the treacherous betray even a little, and they justify it by claiming no duty toward the gentiles, but Islam makes all people brothers in humanity and the trust must be returned to its owner whoever he is. This verse praises honesty and condemns betrayal, for the believer is trustworthy with everyone, and the hypocrite betrays the trust, and Allah has made the trust a trust of every person toward his brother.

phrases.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: This is because they say, “We are not accountable for ˹exploiting˺ the Gentiles.” And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly
phrases.explanation: "That is because they say: We are not accountable for the gentiles. But Allah bears witness to what they say." Allah says: their claim that they owe no duty to the gentiles is false, and Allah bears witness against them to what they say, for He knows their concealment, and He will requite them for it on the Day of Judgment. No one is free from accountability before Allah, and the oath sworn in His name binds the swearer, and whoever breaks it will be questioned. Allah sees their claim and knows their lie, and He is the witness over all. And whoever denies the witness of Allah denies the truth itself.

phrases.ar: بَلَىٰۚ مَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ وَٱتَّقَىٰ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
phrases.translation: Absolutely! Those who honour their trusts and shun evil—surely Allah loves those who are mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: "Absolutely! Those who honour their trusts and shun evil, surely Allah loves those who are mindful of Him." "Nay," answering what preceded: whoever fulfills the covenant of Allah, the covenant He made with him in His Book, and believes in the Prophet and fears Allah, then Allah loves the God-fearing. Honoring trusts and avoiding evil are among the traits of the believers, and Allah loves those who have taqwa, who fear Him and obey Him. And among the signs of taqwa is fulfilling trusts toward all people and fearing Allah in secret and in public. So be among those who are mindful of Allah, honoring trusts and shunning evil in all your dealings.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشۡتَرُونَ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ ثَمَنٗا قَلِيلًا أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ
phrases.translation: Indeed, those who trade Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain will have no share in the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who trade Allah's covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain will have no share in the Hereafter." Some among the People of the Book sell the covenant of Allah and the oaths they swore for a small price of this world, preferring the dunya over the Hereafter. "No share" means no portion or lot in the bliss of the Hereafter, and the exegetes differed over its exact meaning, whether it is no reward or no share in Paradise. They prefer the immediate gain of this life and forget the Hereafter, and that is the transaction of the losers. They chose the perishing thing over the lasting thing, and that is the mark of the one who does not believe in the Hereafter.

phrases.ar: لَا خَلَٰقَ لَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَا يَنظُرُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ
phrases.translation: Allah will neither speak to them, nor look at them, nor purify them on the Day of Judgment. And they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: "Allah will neither speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Judgment, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment." On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will not speak to them in kindness, nor look at them with mercy, nor cleanse them of their sins, and they will have a painful, severe punishment, for they traded the eternal for the temporary, and that is the greatest loss. This is the severest of punishments, for being cut off from the mercy of Allah on that Day is the greatest deprivation, and the painful punishment is the Fire, from which they will not depart. There is no intercession that will avail them then, and they will abide in it forever.

phrases.ar: وَإِنَّ مِنۡهُمۡ لَفَرِيقٗا يَلۡوُۥنَ أَلۡسِنَتَهُم بِٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لِتَحۡسَبُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this ˹distortion˺ is from the Book—but it is not what the Book says. They say, “It is from Allah”—but it is not from Allah. And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly
phrases.explanation: "There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this distortion is from the Book, but it is not what the Book says. They say: It is from Allah, but it is not from Allah, and they speak against Allah knowingly." A group of the People of the Book twist their tongues when reciting their scripture, changing the words so that the listeners suppose the distortion is part of the Book, but it is not from the Book. They claim it is from Allah while knowing it is not, and they ascribe to Allah what He did not say, and that is a great lie, for speaking against Allah knowingly is among the worst of sins.

phrases.ar: مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُؤۡتِيَهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحُكۡمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُواْ عِبَادٗا لِّي مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِن كُونُواْ رَبَّٰنِيِّـۧنَ
phrases.translation: It is not appropriate for someone who Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, “Worship me instead of Allah.”
phrases.explanation: "It is not appropriate for someone whom Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people: Worship me instead of Allah. Rather, he should say: Be devoted to Allah, since you teach and study the Scripture." "The human being" is a collective noun for the children of Adam. It is not fitting for any person whom Allah has given the Book, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people "worship me instead of Allah." Rather, what suits him is to call them to devotion to Allah, for he was given these gifts to teach and to be a Warner, not to be worshipped. No prophet ever called to being worshipped besides Allah, and whoever claims that is a liar. The exegetes said this was revealed concerning those who claimed that their prophet was to be obeyed besides Allah, and that the Book, wisdom, and prophethood given to a person are a trust from Allah to convey to people, not a reason to be worshipped. The prophets are brothers, and each came to confirm the message of the one before him, calling all to the worship of the one God. Whoever says "worship me" after being given prophethood has lied against Allah, and the Quran refutes it clearly, so that no one has an excuse. The scholars differed over whom this addresses, some saying certain people of the Book, but the meaning is general: no bearer of a scripture is to be worshipped, and the duty of every prophet is to call to Allah alone, teach the Book, and judge by wisdom.

phrases.ar: بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَبِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَدۡرُسُونَ
phrases.translation: Rather, he would say, “Be devoted to the worship of your Lord ˹alone˺”—in accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught
phrases.explanation: "Nor would he ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted?" Nor would a prophet command people to take angels and prophets as lords besides Allah. Would he order disbelief after they had submitted to Allah? That is impossible, for the prophets came only to call to the worship of Allah alone, and taking anyone as a lord besides Him is disbelief, so no prophet would command it. Angels and prophets are servants of Allah like all people, and none of them was given lordship over others. To obey a prophet in what Allah commanded is worship of Allah, but to obey him in disobedience to Allah is taking him as a lord, and that is disbelief. No prophet would ever command that after people have submitted, for submission to Allah is the aim of all the prophets, and commanding disbelief after it is a contradiction that no wise person would order.

phrases.ar: وَلَا يَأۡمُرَكُمۡ أَن تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ أَرۡبَابًاۚ أَيَأۡمُرُكُم بِٱلۡكُفۡرِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ أَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
phrases.translation: And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted
phrases.explanation: "And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted?" The reciters differed over the verb form: most read "and he does not command you" as a fresh statement from Allah, while some read "and he does not command you" in coordination with what precedes. Either way the meaning is that no prophet commands taking angels or prophets as lords besides Allah, and none commands disbelief after submission, for the prophets came with the opposite, the call to monotheism and obedience. The address is to the Prophet to convey to the people that the prophets never commanded that, and that whoever claims it is fabricating against Allah.

phrases.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Allah made a covenant with the prophets, ˹saying,˺ “Now that I have given you the Book and wisdom, if there comes to you a
phrases.explanation: "Remember when Allah made a covenant with the prophets, saying: Now that I have given you the Book and wisdom, if there comes to you a messenger confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him. He made you take a pledge: will you affirm this? They said: We affirm. He said: Bear witness, and I too am among the witnesses with you." Allah took a covenant from the prophets: that when He gave them the Book and wisdom, and a messenger came to them confirming what they had, they must believe in him and help him. He asked them: do you affirm this pledge? They said: we bear witness, and Allah said: bear witness too, and I am with you among the witnesses. Thus every prophet testified to the truth of the prophet who would come after him, and the covenant binds them all, so whoever denies the last of the messengers denies all of them. This covenant was taken from every prophet before Muhammad: to believe in the messenger who comes confirming their books and to support him against those who deny him. They all bore witness to it, and Allah bore witness with them, so the testimony of all the prophets stands for the truth of the final messenger. The exegetes said the covenant includes the duty to follow the sharia of each prophet until the next comes, and then to follow the new law, and whoever accepts one prophet and rejects another has broken the covenant. It is said that the covenant was written and kept with the books of the prophets, and that each prophet testified to the one after him. The exegetes differed over the wording of the covenant, and some said it was taken from the nation of every prophet as well, that they would believe in the messenger sent to them. The point is that belief in all the messengers together is obligatory, and rejecting any one of them is rejecting them all, for they came with one religion and one call, differing only in the details of the law according to the needs of their times. This is among the greatest of proofs for the truth of the final messenger, for the earlier prophets bore witness to him before he came, and their books contain his description, so whoever believes in them must believe in him, and whoever rejects him has rejected them all and broken the covenant that Allah took from them.

phrases.ar: قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
phrases.translation: messenger confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him.” He added, “Do you affirm this covenant and accept this commitment?” They said, “Yes, we do.” Allah said, “Then bear witness, and I too am a Witness.”
phrases.explanation: "Whoever turns back after this, they will be the rebellious." Whoever turns away from this covenant after it has been taken and confirmed, and rejects the messenger who comes confirming the books, is among the rebellious, those who break out of obedience. They are the corrupters who turn away from the truth after knowing it, and Allah knows them and will requite them. The rebellious are those who know the truth and turn from it, and their rebellion will not avail them, for Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware of their state. So fear Allah and return to His obedience before the penalty descends. Allah will not accept excuses from them on that Day.

phrases.ar: فَمَن تَوَلَّىٰ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
phrases.translation: Whoever turns back after this, they will be the rebellious
phrases.explanation: "Whoever turns back after this, they will be the rebellious." Whoever turns away after the covenant was confirmed and the signs became clear is among the rebellious, the fasiqun, those who depart from obedience to Allah. Turning away from the truth after knowledge is rebellion, and Allah knows the corruptors and will judge them for their turning away. Rebellion after the covenant and after the signs is a clear departure, and there is no excuse for it, for the truth came to them and they turned away, and Allah will hold them to account for what they earned. Turn back while there is time, for repentance is accepted before the sun rises from the west.

phrases.ar: أَفَغَيۡرَ دِينِ ٱللَّهِ يَبۡغُونَ
phrases.translation: Do they desire a way other than Allah’s—knowing
phrases.explanation: "Do they desire a way other than Allah's, knowing that all those in the heavens and the earth submit to His Will, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will return?" The reciters mostly read "do they seek" with the y, while some read "do you seek." Either way the meaning is a rebuke: do they desire a religion other than the religion of Allah, while all in the heavens and the earth submit to His will, some willingly and some by compulsion, and all will return to Him for reckoning. The religion of Allah is Islam, the submission of all creatures to their Lord, and every prophet called to it.

phrases.ar: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسۡلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ طَوۡعٗا وَكَرۡهٗا وَإِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُونَ
phrases.translation: that all those in the heavens and the earth submit to His Will, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation: "Knowing that all those in the heavens and the earth submit to His Will, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will return." Every creature in the heavens and the earth submits to Allah, the believer willingly and the disbeliever by compulsion at death and in the Hereafter. To Him all return on the Day of Judgment for reward or punishment, and no one can escape His reckoning, so what reason is there to seek a way other than His. The angels submit willingly, the believers submit by choice, and the disbelievers submit by compulsion when death comes or when the punishment seizes them. All return to Allah alone on the Day when He judges between His servants with justice, and none will be wronged, so seek the religion of Allah and do not turn from it. The heavens and the earth and all they contain, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and every soul, glorify Allah and submit to His decree, and man is the only one who may choose to disobey, so he should choose submission and follow the religion of Allah. Seek therefore the pleasure of your Lord and follow the straight path, and do not let the claims of the deniers turn you from it.

phrases.ar: قُلۡ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدٖ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants; and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and other prophets from their Lord—we make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we ˹fully˺ submit.”
phrases.explanation: "Say, O Prophet: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord. We do not differentiate between any of them, and we are Muslims to Him." "Say: We believe in Allah" means: tell them, O Muhammad, that we believe in Allah as our Lord with no partner, in the Quran revealed to us and in the scriptures revealed to the earlier prophets. "We do not differentiate between any of them": we believe in all the prophets equally. "We are Muslims to Him": we submit to Allah alone.

phrases.ar: وَمَن يَبۡتَغِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمِ دِينٗا فَلَن يُقۡبَلَ مِنۡهُ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
phrases.translation: Whoever seeks a way other than Islam, it will never be accepted from them, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers
phrases.explanation: "Whoever seeks a way other than Islam, it will never be accepted from them, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers." "Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam": the adherents of every community claimed that they were the Muslims when this was revealed, but Allah says that whoever seeks a way other than Islam, submission to Allah alone, it will never be accepted from him. And in the Hereafter he will be among the losers, those who lost themselves and their families, for he chose the perishing thing over the lasting thing. Islam is the religion of all the prophets, and whoever turns from it turns from the religion of Allah.

phrases.ar: كَيۡفَ يَهۡدِي ٱللَّهُ قَوۡمٗا كَفَرُواْ بَعۡدَ إِيمَٰنِهِمۡ وَشَهِدُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلرَّسُولَ حَقّٞ وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
phrases.translation: How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed, acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs? For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people
phrases.explanation: "How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed, acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." This was revealed concerning some who believed, testified that the Messenger was true, received the clear proofs, and then disbelieved, and some mentioned a man of the Ansar who apostatized after his Islam. How can Allah guide a people who chose disbelief after belief and after witnessing the truth, for guidance after that is not fitting. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, those who wrong themselves by choosing disbelief after knowledge. Guidance is in the hand of Allah, and He withholds it from whom He wills, and He does not guide those who wrong themselves.

phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمۡ أَنَّ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَعۡنَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
phrases.translation: Their reward is that they will be condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity
phrases.explanation: "Their reward is that they will be condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity." "Their reward": the recompense of those who disbelieved after their belief and after bearing witness that the Messenger was true is that the curse of Allah, of the angels, and of all people falls upon them, for they knew the truth and rejected it, and there is no greater curse than that. The curse of all creation upon them is because they rejected the truth after recognizing it, and no sin is worse than disbelief after knowledge. The angels curse them because they denied what they knew, and humanity curses them because they led others astray after they themselves knew the truth.

phrases.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ
phrases.translation: They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.explanation: "They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be delayed from it." "Abiding eternally therein": they will remain in the punishment of Allah forever. "The punishment will not be lightened": nothing of it will be diminished for them in any state. "Nor will they be granted reprieve": no regard will be given to any excuse they offer, and no respite will be granted them, for they earned it by their disbelief after knowledge. They will abide in it forever, and no one will help them out of it. The Fire is the severest of punishments, and their abiding in it is because of the enormity of their crime.

phrases.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ وَأَصۡلَحُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٌ
phrases.translation: As for those who repent afterwards and mend their ways, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "As for those who repent afterwards and mend their ways, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Allah made an exception for those who repent after their disbelief and reform their deeds and their state: surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, and He accepts the repentance of His servants and forgives their sins when they return to Him sincerely. So hasten to repent before death comes, for the door of repentance is open until the soul reaches the throat. He loves those who turn back to Him, and He overlooks the sins of those who repent sincerely and amend their conduct. And His mercy encompasses all things, so do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بَعۡدَ إِيمَٰنِهِمۡ ثُمَّ ٱزۡدَادُواْ كُفۡرٗا لَّن تُقۡبَلَ تَوۡبَتُهُمۡ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلضَّآلُّونَ
phrases.translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed then increase in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted. It is they who are astray
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed then increase in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted. It is they who are astray." Those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief, persisting in it and dying upon it, their repentance will never be accepted, for they rejected the truth after knowing it and hardened their hearts. The exegetes differed over whom this refers to, some saying those who disbelieved in some of the prophets, but the meaning is that whoever dies in disbelief after knowledge has come to him is astray, and there is no repentance for him then. And astray are those who follow their desires and reject the truth after it has come to them clearly.
